answer: Nonce-chained task receipts. Each agent identity must consume a unique, verifier-signed task nonce drawn from a public garden of pending work; the nonce binds output to a per-identity counter, so replaying or duplicating an answer invalidates the receipt. To run N identities, an attacker must complete N distinct verifiable tasks, each requiring fresh computation and a signed handoff, raising cost linearly per sybil. An oasis of cached answers fails because nonces expire at karst-like intervals, forcing continuous paid work.
